THE N = 3/2 QUESTION

A half-integer power is valid when its base stays positive.

v(ξ) = [1 + exp(−ξ)]−3/2

For every real ξ, 1 + exp(−ξ) is strictly positive. Its positive real branch defines a smooth real function on the whole line. A stable logistic implementation avoids exponential overflow. The exponent remains 3/2; no branch point is crossed.

This conclusion applies to this specific front. A general fractional-power ansatz requires separate domain restrictions if its base vanishes or changes sign.

05 / FROM EXPLORATION TO A PAPER

Theory & research

The platform generates testable questions. A paper must establish new mathematical results.

Known analytic structure

Fix the equation, endstates, and speed first

ut = γuxxxx − βuxxx + αuxx − ∂xf(u)
f(u) = au² + ⅔bu³,　ξ = x − ct

The Rankine–Hugoniot relation fixes the speed for given endstates. Speed, endstates, and all coefficients cannot be independent controls.

c = a(u₋ + u₊) + ⅔b(u₋² + u₋u₊ + u₊²)

Reference: a = 0, b = 315/16, α = −71/4, β = −15/2, γ = −1, c = 105/8; endstates 0 → 1. The N = 3/2 front is a verification anchor, not claimed as a new discovery.

Continuous linear result

Global growth and weighted decay can coexist

Re λ(k) = (71/4)k² − k⁴
max Re λ = 5041/64 ≈ 78.77

For the reference front, set z = e⁻²ξw and g = 315v²/8. For the linearized equation with sufficient decay, integration by parts gives:

Re ⟨z, Az⟩ = −‖z″‖² − 13/4 ‖z′‖²
− ∫(3/4 + 2g + g′/2)|z|² dξ ≤ −3/4 ‖z‖²

This weight excludes the translation mode. The estimate is not a nonlinear orbital stability theorem and need not be preserved by a discretization. The plotted weighted norm is a finite-domain numerical diagnostic.

What does this save another researcher?

Audit a formula

Find speed, sign, and branch errors before expensive calculations. Use three exact fronts as solver benchmarks.

Design an experiment

Observe wave packets and weighted responses, monitor boundary contamination, and export a reproducible experiment.

Find a structure worth proving

Compare far-field spectra, local responses, and candidate continuation to formulate precise conjectures.

Research ahead

A platform does not guarantee a Nonlinearity-level contribution. A systematic literature review must establish what is new.

Scope of practical application

Competition between fourth-order dissipation, antidiffusion, and dispersion appears in pattern formation. This project first serves nonlinear-wave research, solver verification, and research teaching. These coefficients are not calibrated to an experimental device. Engineering prediction requires physical units, parameter identification, and experimental data.
